newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-BACHER MAKES ANOTHER CENTURY IN TVL WIN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BACHER MAKES ANOTHER CENTURY IN TVL WIN.

text.p: Adam Bacher became the first South African batsman to score a century as well as a double century in the same first-class match when Transvaal defeated Griqualand West by 93 runs in Kimberley on Monday.
Bacher added an undefeated 112 to his first innings of 210 to set up victory for Transvaal as Griqualand West were bowled out for 214 after being set a target of 308 for victory.
He became the 35th cricketer to perform the feat, accomplished in 1992 for Northamptonshire by South African-born Allan Lamb who played test cricket for England.

But Ali Bacher, managing director of the United Cricket Board of South Africa -- and Adam Bacher's uncle -- told Reuters the UCB did not regard Lamb as South African. "This is the first time the feat has been performed by a South Afrcan," he said.
Adam Bacher set up a declaration for his side by moving swiftly from his overnight 71 not out to 112 as he and Nic Pothas (37 not out) put on 74 in 16 overs in the first hour of play.
That allowed Transvaal to declare with a lead of 307 and they immediately had the home side in trouble at 32 for three and 115 for five.

A 79-run sixth wicket partnership between Ralph Koster and Cedric English frustrated Transvaal for 90 minutes either side of tea but their separation led to the fall of the final five wickets for only 21 runs.
Bowling: Walsh 21-2-74-2, Roe 13-3-49-1, English 5-0-22-0, Gidley 10-0-31-1, Benkenstein 3-0-13-0
